1.web: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
1.asv: Canst thou draw out leviathan with a fishhook? Or press down his tongue with a cord?

2.web: Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
2.asv: Canst thou put a rope into his nose? Or pierce his jaw through with a hook?

3.web: Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?
3.asv: Will he make many supplications unto thee? Or will he speak soft words unto thee?

4.web: Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?
4.asv: Will he make a covenant with thee, That thou shouldest take him for a servant for ever?

5.web: Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?
5.asv: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? Or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?

6.web: Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?
6.asv: Will the bands of fishermen make traffic of him? Will they part him among the merchants?

7.web: Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?
7.asv: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons, Or his head with fish-spears?

8.web: Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.
8.asv: Lay thy hand upon him; Remember the battle, and do so no more.

9.web: Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won’t one be cast down even at the sight of him?
9.asv: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: Will not one be cast down even at the sight of him?

10.web: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?
10.asv: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up; Who then is he that can stand before me?

11.web: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
11.asv: Who hath first given unto me, that I should repay him? Whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.

12.web: “I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
12.asv: I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, Nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.

13.web: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall come within his jaws?
13.asv: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall come within his jaws?

14.web: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
14.asv: Who can open the doors of his face? Round about his teeth is terror.

15.web: Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.
15.asv: Hisstrong scales are his pride, Shut up together as with a close seal.

16.web: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
16.asv: One is so near to another, That no air can come between them.

17.web: They are joined one to another. They stick together, so that they can’t be pulled apart.
17.asv: They are joined one to another; They stick together, so that they cannot be sundered.

18.web: His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
18.asv: His sneezings flash forth light, And his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

19.web: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap out.
19.asv: Out of his mouth go burning torches, And sparks of fire leap forth.

20.web: Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.
20.asv: Out of his nostrils a smoke goeth, As of a boiling pot and burning rushes.

21.web: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes out of his mouth.
21.asv: His breath kindleth coals, And a flame goeth forth from his mouth.

22.web: There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.
22.asv: In his neck abideth strength, And terror danceth before him.

23.web: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can’t be moved.
23.asv: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: They are firm upon him; they cannot be moved.

24.web: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.
24.asv: His heart is as firm as a stone; Yea, firm as the nether millstone.

25.web: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.
25.asv: When he raiseth himself up, the mighty are afraid: By reason of consternation they are beside themselves.

26.web: If one attacks him with the sword, it can’t prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.
26.asv: If one lay at him with the sword, it cannot avail; Nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.

27.web: He counts iron as straw; and brass as rotten wood.
27.asv: He counteth iron as straw, And brass as rotten wood.

28.web: The arrow can’t make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.
28.asv: The arrow cannot make him flee: Sling-stones are turned with him into stubble.

29.web: Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.
29.asv: Clubs are counted as stubble: He laugheth at the rushing of the javelin.

30.web: His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
30.asv: His underparts are like sharp potsherds: He spreadeth as it were a threshing-wain upon the mire.

31.web: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
31.asv: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: He maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.

32.web: He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.
32.asv: He maketh a path to shine after him; One would think the deep to be hoary.

33.web: On earth there is not his equal, that is made without fear.
33.asv: Upon earth there is not his like, That is made without fear.

34.web: He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride.”
34.asv: He beholdeth everything that is high: He is king over all the sons of pride.
